In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of volcanic ash layers in the upper part of the Cretaceous pelagic and turbidity limestones of the Umbrian Basin (central Apennine), and with the numerical age of the early Campania.
the recognition, correlation and age of two bentonite layers in pelagic and turbidiitic/pelagic successions of the Central Apemnines, which are dated to the early Campania.

(1) the discovery of two discrete bentonite layers intercalated in Upper Cretaceous limestones of the Central Apemnines, (2) their age and correlation, (3) their U/Pb dating, and (4) their petrography and mineralogy.

the volcanic ash layers are a marker horizon for a time interval of 1.2 million years (81.6–80.4 Ma) in the early Campanians and can be used as a stratigraphic tool to constrain the age of the Scaglia facies in the Umbrian basin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a major volcanic event occurred in the late Cretaceous, and that the volcanic ashes were deposited in the Umbrian basin, which was then at its maximum depth, and were preserved in the Scaglia facies, which is the most complete and continuous record of the pelagic sedimentation in this basin.
these bentonite layers provide a new and reliable numerical age for the beginning of the Campanian, which is of interest to many fields of geology.
the bentonite layers at Montagna della Maiela and Gola del Furto are the first volcanic ashes of the early Campanians to be recognized in the Central Apennine basins.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the volcanic ashes are of the same age as the reversed interval of the geomagnetic field, and thus that the reversed interval is not a short-lived event but rather a normal part of the long-term behaviour of the geomagnetic polarity field.
the volcanic ash layers are a reliable time marker for the early Campanion, and can be used for correlation and age dating of Upper Cretaceous successions in the Central Apennine area.
the bentonite seams can be used as time markers to date the pelagic and turbitic limestones of the Umbrian and other basins of the Central Apemnines.
